title: Present a Combined Proposal and Check Its Status
status: New proposed Lesson 08 production script, 2026-10-30. No new animation or narration in this handoff.
learningOutcome: Present a combined candidate, ask a focused support check and update only the status actually supported by the authored replies.

scenario.kind: Original fictional discussion-training case with explicitly named snapshots
scenario.sourcePrompt: A community book club wants a 30-minute taster activity for new readers. Help them try discussing a short text and find out how the weekly club works. Your group should recommend one coherent activity and explain how it serves both aims. Use the main room, the supplied one-page text and club information sheet, and existing paper and pens; do not buy anything. Leave at least five minutes within the session for visitors' questions.

facts.text: The task is one coherent 30-minute taster activity, serving both trying a short-text discussion and learning how the weekly club works.
The main room, one supplied one-page text, a club information sheet, paper and pens are available. No purchases are allowed. At least five minutes for questions is included within the thirty minutes.
Maya proposes: Pairs could compare one line from the short text before we share anything with the whole group.
Noah proposes: A short demonstration could show newcomers what it means to give an interpretation and a reason.
The participant proposes: I suggest keeping time for questions about the club, using the information sheet for anything it actually answers.
Maya states partial support: I support showing an example, but I don't want it to take away the pair discussion.
Noah states partial support: I support some pair discussion. I still want us to decide how short the demonstration should be.
The participant states: I support protecting the question time. We still need a workable sequence within thirty minutes.
No complete sequence, stage durations or demonstration leader has been agreed. No taster has happened and no visitor result has been measured.

unknowns: The exact stage durations and whether an eventual detailed schedule fits
Who is willing and able to give the example
Which visitor questions the supplied information sheet will answer
Visitors' number, needs, preferences and willingness to share
Whether the group will adopt a complete proposal
How the activity would work in practice

baseline.meaning: All three proposals and the three explicit support statements are available as attributed source cards. The whole proposal remains open. Branch replies never become baseline facts.

proposal_check.proposal: We could begin with a brief example, use the same text in pairs, share one idea, and keep at least five minutes for club questions. Can we check the timing and who would give the example before we decide?
proposal_check.mayaReply: I support that sequence if the demonstration stays brief and the pair task remains.
proposal_check.noahReply: I support starting with an example and keeping question time. I am not ready to agree on the full sequence until we check the timings.
proposal_check.meaning: A labelled later authored check adds exactly these replies. Maya supports the sequence conditionally; Noah supports two elements and withholds support for the whole sequence pending timing. This does not establish a final group decision.

rehearsal.meaning: Use the explicit S05 proposal and replies as a frozen reference board, not as new speech to the learner. A private summary remains blank; the optional model is separate.

boundaries: Partial support attaches to a named element or condition; do not promote it to unconditional whole-group agreement.
No majority rule, unanimous decision procedure, assigned leader or final authority is supplied.
Thirty minutes is the activity duration, not a learner speaking limit or discussion deadline. The five-minute minimum is included, not added after thirty minutes.
At most twenty-five minutes remain for all other stages and transitions together, and fewer if question time exceeds five. This is a bound, not an agreed schedule.
A proposed demonstration leader is an unresolved dependency; do not assign Maya, Noah or an invisible facilitator without an authored decision.
The information sheet exists, but its complete contents are not supplied. Mark an unanswered question for checking; do not invent its answer.
Branch continuations and later model replies are authored examples, not observed real learner behaviour.
A coherent candidate can still need timing, accessibility and participation checks. Do not guarantee that a courteous summary wins agreement.

blocks.title: Bring Back a Candidate People Can Inspect
Ask a Question That Can Change the Record
Choose a Next Check without Assigning Authority

L08.S05.c001.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c001.text: A combined proposal should make its connections easy to follow. Show the main sequence, explain how it serves the aims, and keep the important checks nearby. You are giving people something to inspect, not presenting a polished diagram as proof that the discussion has already reached a decision.
L08.S05.c001.visualEn: Formal candidate sequence board with purpose links and open checks. No agreed stamp or completion animation.
L08.S05.c001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c001.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.c002.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c002.text: This is a later authored check of the book-club candidate. The earlier partial support remains the starting point. The next lines supply new statements for this example only; a person must actually say what they support before their status card changes.
L08.S05.c002.visualEn: Mark a visible snapshot change: Later proposal check. Preserve the baseline ledger separately; do not import any S02/S03 branch outcome.
L08.S05.c002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c002.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.d001.speaker: learner
L08.S05.d001.text: We could begin with a brief example, use the same text in pairs, share one idea, and keep at least five minutes for club questions. Can we check the timing and who would give the example before we decide?
L08.S05.d001.visualEn: Participant proposes the four connected stages, a protected minimum question period, and unresolved timing/person checks. No durations except supplied30/min5 are invented.
L08.S05.d001.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.d001.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L08.S05.c003.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c003.text: The proposed example and pair discussion use the same text, so they are connected stages rather than separate activities competing for a place. Sharing would draw on the pair task. The candidate still needs timing and someone to give the example; mentioning those checks does not mean they have been completed.
L08.S05.c003.visualEn: Carry the same text card across stages, preserving identity. Open timing/person tags stay attached after the speech bubble leaves.
L08.S05.c003.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c003.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.c004.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c004.text: A focused check asks about an element or a condition that is still open. Do you support this sequence, or is there something you would change? That is more useful than asking everyone to approve a summary that already says everyone agrees. Leave space for a limited or negative answer.
L08.S05.c004.visualEn: The support ledger opens editable status cells, including conditional and unresolved states, without default selection.
L08.S05.c004.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c004.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.d002.speaker: maya
L08.S05.d002.text: I support that sequence if the demonstration stays brief and the pair task remains.
L08.S05.d002.visualEn: Maya gives the exact conditional support. Move only Maya's status card, retaining both conditions beside it.
L08.S05.d002.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.d002.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L08.S05.c005.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c005.text: Maya has now supported the sequence, with conditions. Record the whole statement: the example stays brief and the pair task remains. Do not turn it into unconditional support, and do not treat her response as an answer to who would lead the example.
L08.S05.c005.visualEn: Maya row updates to conditional support; timing and leader rows do not change.
L08.S05.c005.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c005.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.d003.speaker: noah
L08.S05.d003.text: I support starting with an example and keeping question time. I am not ready to agree on the full sequence until we check the timings.
L08.S05.d003.visualEn: Noah's support applies only to starting with an example and protecting question time; full sequence remains withheld pending timing.
L08.S05.d003.anchorHint: not ready to agree on the full sequence
L08.S05.d003.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.d003.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L08.S05.c006.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c006.text: Noah's reply is not a rejection of every part. It preserves support for two elements and gives a reason for withholding support for the complete arrangement. Your summary should be able to hold that mixed position without colouring the whole row simply yes or no.
L08.S05.c006.visualEn: Noah row contains supported elements plus open whole-sequence status. Use words and separate cards, not binary red/green coding.
L08.S05.c006.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c006.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.c007.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c007.text: The current record has moved forward, but it is still not a final group decision. A useful next step is to draft stage lengths, include transitions and protect the question period, then ask whether the result addresses the reservation. Someone also needs to check who could give the example.
L08.S05.c007.visualEn: Show updated support ledger beside two unresolved next checks. Do not auto-assign either task or mark them completed.
L08.S05.c007.anchorHint: still not a final group decision
L08.S05.c007.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c007.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.c008.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c008.text: If you offer to make that draft, present it as an offer rather than a command. Nothing in this case appoints a leader or establishes a voting rule. The group can decide how to do the check; the summariser should not quietly claim authority over that decision.
L08.S05.c008.visualEn: Optional offer card, no leader badge, role assignment or majority tally.
L08.S05.c008.anchorHint: an offer rather than a command
L08.S05.c008.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c008.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.d004.speaker: learner
L08.S05.d004.text: Would it help if we sketched the stage lengths next, including transitions, and then checked whether the sequence fits?
L08.S05.d004.visualEn: Participant offers a focused next check. No peer reply follows, so acceptance remains unknown.
L08.S05.d004.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.d004.delivery: Natural collaborative speech; restrained gesture, no exaggerated conflict or comic voice.

L08.S05.c009.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c009.text: An offer without a reply remains an offer. Keep that distinction when you hand over the summary. Otherwise, a proposed action can quietly become someone's obligation, just as partial support can quietly become consensus.
L08.S05.c009.visualEn: Next-step card is labelled Offered; do not move it into Assigned or Done.
L08.S05.c009.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c009.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.c010.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c010.text: A helpful handover lets someone see the candidate, whose support is conditional, what remains unresolved and what check is being proposed. Keep it concise enough to use, but not so short that the conditions disappear. The next speaker should be able to correct one item without rebuilding the whole account.
L08.S05.c010.visualEn: Compress the ledger into a four-line draft summary, all explicit conditions retained and original sources reachable.
L08.S05.c010.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c010.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.c011.speaker: coach
L08.S05.c011.text: The point of checking is not to collect a polite yes. It is to make the group's actual position clear enough for a useful next decision. In the next section, practise giving that kind of summary while keeping your own private rehearsal separate from the authored example.
L08.S05.c011.visualEn: End with clear partial/open status, then a blank rehearsal card that is not prefilled.
L08.S05.c011.textStatus: Original proposed exact script; not recorded audio, an observed learner answer, or an official assessment.
L08.S05.c011.delivery: Calm, concrete teaching; emphasis follows the semantic distinction, with natural pauses.

L08.S05.h101.purpose: Privately identify which part of the candidate is established by the prompt and which part still needs a group decision.
L08.S05.h101.visualEn: Fixed requirement and candidate rails remain separate; private response stays blank.

L08.S05.h102.purpose: Privately summarise Maya's support, Noah's reservation and one possible next check.
L08.S05.h102.visualEn: Three blank private note rows. Exact authored replies stay accessible as reference, not as a completed learner response.

boundary: Use formal explanation and short explicitly fictional excerpts. Partial support, open questions, candidate proposals and adopted decisions stay distinct. A summary does not create consent. Models are separate authored examples, not captured learner speech.
